categories.name: Geopolitical & conflict

sources.title: Euronews: Iran attacks US bases in Bahrain as its tankers get ready to break the US blockade
Gulf News: Trump threatens to sink Iranian vessels
Al Jazeera: Russian missiles hit Poland

categories.summary: No new tanker hits were confirmed since the two off Oman on 21 November. Bahrain says it intercepted Iranian attacks on US bases on 21 November, and Iran is readying a tanker convoy at Kharg Island to test the US blockade, with Trump threatening to sink Iranian vessels: a possible flashpoint in the coming days. Poland and NATO have not responded militarily to the Russian missiles of 20 November. Taiwan and Korea are quiet.

categories.name: Nuclear & fallout
categories.summary: US nuclear-command and tanker aircraft are normal. Forecast markets put a Russian or US nuclear test this year at about 2-3%.

categories.name: Cyber & infrastructure

sources.title: iTnews: Storage failure downs New Zealand Defence websites
NZ Herald: NZ Defence Force sites offline

categories.summary: The run of big overseas outages and hacks continues (Chase, Apple, Visa/Mastercard suppliers, the FBI database, Microsoft, Delta). New Zealand Defence Force websites are still down; one report blames a storage failure, and a claimed data breach is not confirmed. ASX-listed Peninsula Energy reported a cyber incident at its US mine in Wyoming, with no effect here. The collector's link of China-linked hacking to Australia still rests on a news story about Australia-China talks, not an attack here. Australian phones, banks and the grid are normal.

categories.name: Pandemic & biological

sources.title: WHO: Ebola (Bundibugyo) - DRC, Kenya and Nigeria

categories.summary: WHO reports Ebola in DR Congo, Kenya and Nigeria and MERS in Qatar and Saudi Arabia; none is spreading toward Australia. A stomach bug on a US cruise ship and a US crash are not health threats to us. Only one Adelaide emergency department is very busy, which is normal.

categories.name: Natural hazards

sources.title: Bureau of Meteorology: SA fire danger ratings

categories.summary: Fire danger in the Mount Lofty Ranges was High today and drops to Moderate on Tuesday; Wednesday warms to about 28°C. No fire bans, CFS warnings or Watch and Act messages near home. A magnitude 6.5 quake in the South Pacific poses no tsunami threat to SA. Some outback roads in the north-east remain closed by earlier flooding, far from home.

categories.name: Fuel, food & supply

sources.title: Khaleej Times: Oil falls almost 5% as Trump signals restraint on Iran

categories.summary: Hormuz is still effectively shut (100+ ships a day before the war; about 2 a day now). Brent oil fell to about US$90 and SA pump prices are a few cents lower than last week. Supply is tight but there are no shortages in SA; the tanker convoy standoff could push prices up again.

categories.name: Markets & finance
categories.summary: The US 'fear gauge' (VIX) is about 36, gold rose about 3% and the Australian dollar is about 66 US cents. Jittery, but no sign of a crash or bank trouble in Australia.

headline: Iran is lining up oil tankers to run the US blockade and Trump has threatened to sink them, so Hormuz could flare up again; no new hits on ships confirmed today.
summary: No new tanker hits were confirmed today, but Iran is gathering a convoy of oil tankers at Kharg Island to test the US blockade and President Trump has threatened to sink Iranian ships; Bahrain says it shot down Iranian attacks on US bases on Saturday. Today's 'power outage in SA' phone alerts were a false alarm caused by news stories, already corrected: the SA grid is normal. Overseas, Belgium closed its airspace for the day because of a strike, not an attack. Fire danger in the Hills drops to Moderate on Tuesday, and Australian phones and banks are working normally.
